## Question and parity rules

How do mean BMI, sample standard deviation, and the number of observations vary by income group and gender among adults aged 20–80? Both languages use the same cached CSV, remove rows missing BMI or either grouping variable, restrict age to 20–80 inclusive, calculate sample SD, and round mean and SD to one decimal place.

## Load and inspect

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

nhanes <- read_csv(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

raw_check <- tibble(
  rows = nrow(nhanes),
  columns = ncol(nhanes),
  missing_bmi = sum(is.na(nhanes$BMI))
)
raw_check
```

## R pipeline

```{r}
bmi_by_group_pipeline <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Gender),
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80
  ) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
    sd_bmi = sd(BMI),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 1),
    sd_bmi = round(sd_bmi, 1)
  )

bmi_by_group_pipeline
```

## Reusable R function

The function accepts a data frame and inclusive age bounds, so the same summary can be reused without copying the filtering and grouping logic.

```{r}
summarize_bmi_by_group <- function(data, age_min = 20, age_max = 80) {
  data |>
    filter(
      !is.na(BMI),
      !is.na(IncomeGroup),
      !is.na(Gender),
      Age >= age_min,
      Age <= age_max
    ) |>
    group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_bmi = mean(BMI),
      sd_bmi = sd(BMI),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      mean_bmi = round(mean_bmi, 1),
      sd_bmi = round(sd_bmi, 1)
    )
}

bmi_by_group_function <- summarize_bmi_by_group(nhanes)
stopifnot(identical(bmi_by_group_pipeline, bmi_by_group_function))
bmi_by_group_function
```

## Parity checks

```{r}
filtered_rows <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(IncomeGroup),
    !is.na(Gender),
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80
  ) |>
  nrow()

parity_metrics <- tibble(
  metric = c("raw_row_count", "raw_column_count", "missing_BMI", "filtered_row_count", "number_of_groups"),
  r_value = c(nrow(nhanes), ncol(nhanes), sum(is.na(nhanes$BMI)), filtered_rows, nrow(bmi_by_group_pipeline))
)
parity_metrics

parity_table <- read_csv(
  "assignments/assignment04-polyglot/submission/parity-table.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
parity_table
```

The detailed rounded values and corresponding pandas results are recorded in `parity-table.csv`. The Python notebook uses pandas' sample standard deviation (`ddof=1`), matching R's `sd()`.
